problem: Object navigation systems usually treat semantic segmentation and navigation policy as separate modules, using single-frame segmentation that ignores temporal context. Transformer-based navigation policies are also sample-inefficient and computationally heavy.
motivation: Reaching targets given by semantic category requires robust perception and decision-making, and errors in single-frame segmentation propagate to the policy. Temporal information from sequential observations could improve both segmentation and action selection if they are trained jointly.
key_idea: SegDT is a Decision Transformer that jointly predicts semantic segmentation masks and navigation actions from an observation sequence, trained with offline pretraining on expert demonstrations followed by online refinement via knowledge transfer from an RNN policy.
insight: Tight coupling of segmentation and navigation lets temporal context improve both tasks; the abstract says ablations show temporal processing improves segmentation quality. The two-phase training (offline pretraining, then online refinement with RNN knowledge transfer) addresses the transformer's sample inefficiency. Details of the ablations are not available from the abstract.
method: Joint transformer model: a Decision Transformer that outputs semantic segmentation masks and navigation actions together.
Temporal processing: uses sequences of past observations to improve both segmentation and action prediction.
Offline pretraining: trained on expert demonstrations.
Online refinement: policy fine-tuned online through knowledge transfer from a recurrent neural network policy.
Integration: plugged into complete object navigation systems, giving a 9.6% gain in path efficiency over the state of the art.

setting.training_data: Expert demonstrations for offline pretraining, then online RL in Habitat with RNN teacher distillation; scale not stated in the abstract
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB (and probably depth) sequences; not fully specified in the abstract
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level actions (not specified in the abstract)
setting.privileged: none stated (ground-truth semantics only used in a comparison upper bound)

results: SegDT with predicted segmentation masks outperforms a single-frame baseline using a pre-trained segmentation model and approaches systems using ground-truth semantics. When integrated into complete object navigation systems, it improves path efficiency by 9.6% over the state-of-the-art method.
limitations: Evaluated only in the Habitat simulator; no real-robot results are reported in the abstract.
Requires a two-phase training pipeline with expert demonstrations and an RNN teacher.
compares_to: Single-frame baseline with pre-trained semantic segmentation
